q: A plant disease is usually defined as abnormal _____ and/or dysfunction of a plant.
e: A plant disease is usually defined as abnormal growth and/or dysfunction of a plant.

q: Biotic diseases are caused by _____ organisms.
e: Biotic diseases are caused by living organisms such as fungi, bacteria, and viruses.

q: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living _____ conditions.
e: Abiotic diseases are caused by non-living environmental conditions.

q: Most plant diseases, around _____ percent are caused by fungal or fungal-like organisms.
e: Most plant diseases, around 85 percent, are caused by fungal or fungal-like organisms.

q: Nematodes are very tiny _____.
e: Nematodes are very tiny roundworms that act as plant parasites.

q: The study of plant diseases is called plant _____.
e: The study of plant diseases is called plant pathology.

q: Pathology is derived from the Greek word pathos which means suffering or _____.
e: Pathos means suffering or disease in Greek.

q: Pathology is derived from the Greek word logos which means discourse or _____.
e: Logos means discourse or study in Greek.

q: Plant diseases occurrence and severity result from the impact of _____ factors represented in the disease triangle.
e: The disease triangle represents the impact of three factors: host, pathogen, and environment.

q: The disease triangle includes the host plant, the pathogen and the _____ conditions.
e: The three factors are the host plant, the pathogen, and the environmental conditions.

q: Signs of plant disease are _____ evidence of the pathogen.
e: Signs of plant disease are physical evidence of the pathogen.

q: Symptoms are visible _____ of disease on plants.
e: Symptoms are visible effects of disease on plants.

q: Because viruses are systemic, infected plants must be _____ or discarded.
e: Because viruses are systemic, infected plants must be rogued or discarded.

q: Fungi and fungal-like organisms cause more plant diseases than any other group with over _____ species shown to cause disease.
e: Over 8,000 species of fungi and fungal-like organisms are shown to cause disease.

q: There are approximately _____ types of bacteria that cause diseases in plants.
e: There are approximately 200 types of bacteria that cause diseases in plants.

q: The presence of a _____ is the key diagnostic sign differentiating plant parasitic nematodes from all other types.
e: The presence of a stylet is the key diagnostic sign for plant parasitic nematodes.

q: There are _____ plant diseases control approaches: biological, physical and chemical.
e: There are three plant diseases control approaches: biological, physical, and chemical.

q: Biological control is control of plant diseases using living _____.
e: Biological control uses living microorganisms to control plant diseases.

q: In biological control, an antagonist may secrete metabolites harmful to the pathogens, which is called _____.
e: Secretion of harmful metabolites by an antagonist is called antibiosis.

q: In biological control, an antagonist may cause death of the parasite by producing enzymes, a process called _____.
e: Causing death of the parasite by producing enzymes is called lysis.

q: Chemicals used to control bacteria are called _____.
e: Chemicals used to control bacteria are called bactericides.

q: Chemicals used to control fungi are called _____.
e: Chemicals used to control fungi are called fungicides.

q: Chemicals used to control nematodes are called _____.
e: Chemicals used to control nematodes are called nematicides.

q: Abiotic diseases do not show the presence of disease _____.
e: Abiotic diseases do not show the presence of disease signs.

q: Fungi that cause tomato leaf blight do not cause damage on sweet corn, showing biotic problems are limited to a certain _____.
e: Biotic disease problems are more limited to a certain species.

q: Alternaria genus of fungi causes leaf spots and _____ of various plants.
e: Alternaria causes leaf spots and blight of various plants.

q: Aspergillus genus of fungi causes _____ of seeds.
e: Aspergillus causes rots of seeds.

q: Puccinia genus of fungi causes _____ of cereals.
e: Puccinia causes rust of cereals.

q: Rhizopus genus of fungi causes soft rot of _____.
e: Rhizopus causes soft rot of fruits.

q: Sclerotinia genus of fungi causes soft rot of _____.
e: Sclerotinia causes soft rot of vegetables.

q: Most plant pathogenic bacteria are most active in warm and _____ environments.
e: Plant pathogenic bacteria are most active in warm and humid environments.

q: Agrobacterium, Erwinia, and Pseudomonas are genera of plant pathogenic _____.
e: These are genera of plant pathogenic bacteria.

q: Nematodes are simple, multicellular animals and are bilaterally symmetrical, soft-bodied, non-segmented _____.
e: Nematodes are non-segmented roundworms.

q: Wheat nematode is scientifically known as Anguina _____.
e: Wheat nematode is Anguina tritici.

q: Spring dwarf nematode is scientifically known as Aphelenchoides _____.
e: Spring dwarf nematode is Aphelenchoides fragariae.

q: Root-knot nematodes belong to the genus _____.
e: Root-knot nematodes belong to the genus Meloidogyne.

q: Physical methods of disease control are based on the physiological tolerance of disease agents to _____ conditions.
e: Physical control relies on tolerance to adverse conditions.

q: An infectious agent is capable of reproducing within or on its host and spreading from one susceptible host to _____.
e: Infectious agents spread from one susceptible host to another.

q: Non-infectious plant diseases are caused by unfavorable growing conditions and are not _____.
e: Non-infectious causal agents are not transmissible.

q: Viruses cause mottling, spots, and _____-like patterns on leaves and fruits.
e: Viruses cause mosaic-like patterns on leaves and fruits.

q: Bacterial ooze and nematode cysts are examples of disease _____.
e: Bacterial ooze and nematode cysts are physical evidence, hence signs.

q: Blight, canker, and chlorosis are examples of plant disease _____.
e: Blight, canker, and chlorosis are visible effects, hence symptoms.

q: The genus Fusarium causes _____ rot of many plants.
e: Fusarium causes root rot of many plants.

q: Botrytis genus causes _____ of various plants.
e: Botrytis causes blights of various plants.

q: Curly top virus and cucumber mosaic virus are common virus diseases in _____.
e: These are common virus diseases in tomatoes.
